items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials with Option-Indexed Variables
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (a : σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf a p =
    ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R { b // b ≠ a })
        ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(Equiv.optionSubtypeNe a).symm) p)).natDegree
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \text{Option } \sigma $, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $. This equivalence maps variables corresponding to $ \text{none} $ to the outer polynomial indeterminate and variables corresponding to $ \text{some } s $ to coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring, with the inverse given by variable substitution.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence between Multivariate Polynomials over Option σ and Polynomials in One Variable with Multivariate Coefficients
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R),
  ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) p).natDegree = MvPolynomial.degreeOf none p
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ (i.e., $\sigma \cup \{\text{none}\}$) and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable (corresponding to $\text{none}$) whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence maps variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ to either the outer polynomial's indeterminate (for $\text{none}$) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for $\text{some } s$), with the inverse given by renaming variables.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence Between Multivariate Polynomials Over Option σ and Polynomials in One Variable with Multivariate Coefficients
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {f : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R},
  f ≠ 0 → ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) f).degree = ↑(MvPolynomial.degreeOf none f)
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence maps variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ to either the indeterminate of the outer polynomial ring (for the $\text{none}$ case) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for the $\text{some } s$ cases), with the inverse given by substituting renamed variables. For any nonzero polynomial $f$, the degree of the transformed polynomial equals the total degree of $f$ in the $\text{none}$ variable.

items.informal_name: Injective Renaming Preserves Variable Degree in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (i : σ), MvPolynomial.degreeOf (f i) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, the total degree of the variable $ f(i) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \operatorname{rename}(f, p) $ equals the total degree of the variable $ i $ in the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \deg_{f(i)}(\operatorname{rename}(f, p)) = \deg_i(p) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Polynomial Evaluation in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} (f : σ → τ) (i : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((Polynomial.aeval (MvPolynomial.X i)) p) = (Polynomial.aeval (MvPolynomial.X (f i))) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, variable $ i \in \sigma $, and polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, renaming the variables in the evaluation of $ p $ at $ X_i $ via $ f $ yields the same result as evaluating $ p $ at the renamed variable $ X_{f(i)} $ in $ R[\tau] $. Formally, $ \text{rename} \, f \, (\text{aeval}(X_i, p)) = \text{aeval}(X_{f(i)}, p) $.

items.name: Polynomial.natDegree_mul
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] [NoZeroDivisors R] {p q : Polynomial R},
  p ≠ 0 → q ≠ 0 → (p * q).natDegree = p.natDegree + q.natDegree

items.name: Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_mul'
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p q : Polynomial R}, p.Monic → q ≠ 0 → (p * q).natDegree = p.natDegree + q.natDegree

items.name: MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_eq
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {n : σ} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p q : MvPolynomial σ R} [NoZeroDivisors R],
  p ≠ 0 → q ≠ 0 → MvPolynomial.degreeOf n (p * q) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf n p + MvPolynomial.degreeOf n q

items.name: MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_X_of_ne
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i j : σ} (f : MvPolynomial σ R),
  i ≠ j → MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (f * MvPolynomial.X j) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf i f

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence between Multivariate Polynomials over Option σ and Polynomials in One Variable with Multivariate Coefficients
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R),
  ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) p).natDegree = MvPolynomial.degreeOf none p
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ (i.e., $\sigma \cup \{\text{none}\}$) and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable (corresponding to $\text{none}$) whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence maps variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ to either the outer polynomial's indeterminate (for $\text{none}$) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for $\text{some } s$), with the inverse given by renaming variables.

items.informal_name: Algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over Option σ and polynomials in one variable with multivariate coefficients
items.type: (R : Type u) → (S₁ : Type v) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → MvPolynomial (Option S₁) R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial (MvPolynomial S₁ R)
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence is constructed by evaluating variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ as either the indeterminate of the outer polynomial ring (for the $\text{none}$ case) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for the $\text{some } s$ cases), with the inverse given by substituting the renamed variables.

items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence Between Multivariate Polynomials Over Option σ and Polynomials in One Variable with Multivariate Coefficients
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {f : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R},
  f ≠ 0 → ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) f).degree = ↑(MvPolynomial.degreeOf none f)
items.informal_description: There exists an algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Option } \sigma$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$. This equivalence maps variables in $\text{Option } \sigma$ to either the indeterminate of the outer polynomial ring (for the $\text{none}$ case) or coefficients in the inner multivariate polynomial ring (for the $\text{some } s$ cases), with the inverse given by substituting renamed variables. For any nonzero polynomial $f$, the degree of the transformed polynomial equals the total degree of $f$ in the $\text{none}$ variable.

items.informal_name: Application of Algebra Equivalence for Optional Variables in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) (S₁ : Type v) [inst : CommSemiring R] (a : MvPolynomial (Option S₁) R),
  (MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R S₁) a =
    (MvPolynomial.aeval fun o => o.elim Polynomial.X fun s => Polynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X s)) a
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over $\text{Option } \sigma$ and polynomials in one variable with multivariate coefficients over $\sigma$ is defined by evaluating each variable in $\text{Option } \sigma$ as either the indeterminate of the outer polynomial ring (for the $\text{none}$ case) or as the constant polynomial with coefficient corresponding to the variable in $\sigma$ (for the $\text{some } s$ case).

items.informal_name: Image of $ X_{\text{none}} $ under Option $ \sigma $ Polynomial Equivalence is $ X $
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) (S₁ : Type v) [inst : CommSemiring R],
  (MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R S₁) (MvPolynomial.X none) = Polynomial.X
items.informal_description: Under the algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\text{Option } \sigma] $ and the polynomial ring $ (R[\sigma])[X] $, the variable corresponding to $ \text{none} $ in $ \text{Option } \sigma $ is mapped to the indeterminate $ X $ of the outer polynomial ring.

items.type:

  [inst_2 : FunLike F (Polynomial R) (Polynomial S)] [AddMonoidHomClass F (Polynomial R) (Polynomial S)] {φ : F}
